questions.question_text: In humans, fertilisation most commonly occurs in which part of the female reproductive tract?
questions.explanation: Fertilisation usually occurs in the oviduct; the resulting embryo later travels to the uterus for implantation.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT Biology, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: The finger-like projections near the ovary that help guide a released ovum into the oviduct are called
questions.explanation: Fimbriae at the funnel-shaped end of the oviduct help collect the ovum after ovulation.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT Biology, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: Which event directly restores the diploid chromosome number in a human zygote?
questions.option_a: Fusion of two haploid gamete nuclei
questions.option_d: Release of an ovum from the ovary
questions.explanation: A haploid sperm nucleus fuses with a haploid ovum nucleus at fertilisation, restoring diploidy.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT Biology, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: A fertilised human egg divides repeatedly while moving toward the uterus. The compact ball of cells eventually develops into a
questions.option_a: blastocyst that can implant in the uterine lining
questions.option_d: mature ovum that leaves through the cervix
questions.explanation: Early cleavage divisions produce a blastocyst, which reaches the uterus and can implant in the endometrium.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT Biology, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: Which statement about the human placenta is correct?
questions.option_a: It allows exchange between maternal and fetal blood without normally making the two blood supplies one circulation
questions.option_b: It is the site where sperm are produced
questions.option_c: It prevents every substance in maternal blood from reaching the fetus
questions.option_d: It directly connects the fetal lungs to outside air
questions.explanation: The placenta mediates exchange of gases, nutrients and wastes; maternal and fetal blood are normally separated by a tissue barrier.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT Biology, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: During pregnancy, the amniotic fluid chiefly helps by
questions.option_a: cushioning the developing fetus against mechanical shocks
questions.option_c: carrying oxygen in red blood cells
questions.explanation: Amniotic fluid surrounds the fetus and provides cushioning and a suitable environment for movement and development.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT Biology, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: The first menstrual bleeding at puberty is known as
questions.explanation: Menarche is the onset of menstruation, marking reproductive maturation at puberty.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT Biology, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: The permanent cessation of menstrual cycles, generally occurring later in life, is termed
questions.explanation: Menopause is the permanent cessation of menstruation due to loss of ovarian follicular activity.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT Biology, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: After ovulation, the ruptured ovarian follicle becomes the corpus luteum. Its progesterone helps
questions.option_a: maintain the uterine lining during the luteal phase
questions.option_b: cause sperm to mature in the epididymis
questions.option_c: trigger milk ejection from the breast
questions.option_d: form the acrosome of the ovum
questions.explanation: The corpus luteum secretes progesterone, supporting the endometrium after ovulation and in early pregnancy.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT Biology, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: A sharp rise in which pituitary hormone is the usual immediate trigger for ovulation?
questions.explanation: The mid-cycle luteinising hormone surge triggers ovulation; follicle-stimulating hormone also contributes to follicular development.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT Biology, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: Which structure in a human sperm contains enzymes that help it penetrate the coverings of the ovum?
questions.explanation: The acrosome at the sperm head contains enzymes involved in penetrating the egg's outer investments.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT Biology, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: In the male reproductive tract, sperm acquire motility and undergo maturation mainly in the
questions.explanation: Sperm are produced in seminiferous tubules and mature while passing through the epididymis.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT Biology, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: Which duct carries sperm from the epididymis toward the urethra?
questions.explanation: The vas deferens transports sperm from the epididymis toward the ejaculatory duct and urethra.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT Biology, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: The seminal vesicles contribute fluid that is rich in a sugar used as an energy source by sperm. Which sugar is it?
questions.explanation: Seminal vesicle secretions contain fructose, which can provide an energy substrate for sperm.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT Biology, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: Testosterone is produced mainly by which cells in the testes?
questions.explanation: Leydig (interstitial) cells produce testosterone; Sertoli cells support developing sperm cells.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT Biology, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: Which testicular cells provide structural and nutritional support to developing sperm cells?
questions.explanation: Sertoli cells in seminiferous tubules support and nourish developing germ cells; Leydig cells produce testosterone.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT Biology, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: Spermatogenesis takes place in which testicular structures?
questions.explanation: Spermatogenesis occurs in the seminiferous tubules of the testes.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT Biology, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: One primary spermatocyte undergoing meiosis can ultimately produce how many haploid spermatids?
questions.explanation: Meiosis of a primary spermatocyte produces four haploid spermatids, which differentiate into spermatozoa.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT Biology, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: Why must human gametes be haploid before fertilisation?
questions.option_a: Their fusion restores the normal diploid chromosome number
questions.option_c: It makes the zygote genetically identical to the mother
questions.option_d: It removes the need for DNA replication
questions.explanation: Meiosis halves chromosome number in gametes so fusion at fertilisation restores the species' diploid number rather than doubling it each generation.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT Biology, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: Which contraceptive method also reduces the risk of transmission of many sexually transmitted infections when used correctly?
questions.explanation: Condoms provide a physical barrier and reduce transmission risk for many STIs; they do not eliminate all risk.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT Biology, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: A vasectomy prevents sperm from entering the semen primarily by cutting or blocking the
questions.explanation: Vasectomy blocks the vas deferens; it does not remove the testes or ordinarily stop testosterone production.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT Biology, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: Tubal ligation (tubectomy) prevents pregnancy mainly by blocking the
questions.option_a: oviducts, limiting the meeting of sperm and ovum
questions.option_d: ovaries, removing all ova from the body
questions.explanation: Tubectomy blocks or cuts the oviducts, preventing gamete transport and fertilisation in most cases.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT Biology, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: A copper intrauterine device primarily reduces the chance of fertilisation by
questions.option_a: creating a local environment that impairs sperm function
questions.option_b: stopping the pituitary from making every hormone
questions.explanation: Copper IUDs release copper ions that impair sperm motility and viability and thereby reduce fertilisation likelihood.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT Biology, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: In Spirogyra, a broken filament can grow into a new individual. Which asexual process does this illustrate?
questions.explanation: Spirogyra can reproduce by fragmentation: a filament breaks into pieces, and each suitable fragment grows into a new filament.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT Biology, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: Under unfavourable conditions, Plasmodium can multiply by repeated nuclear division followed by division of cytoplasm. This is
questions.explanation: Plasmodium can reproduce by multiple fission, producing many daughter cells from one parent cell.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT Biology, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: A detached Planaria fragment forms a complete organism. This outcome is best associated with
questions.explanation: Planaria can regenerate lost parts, and fragments under suitable conditions can develop into complete individuals.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT Biology, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: A farmer plants a potato tuber piece containing an eye. The new plant arises through
questions.option_a: vegetative propagation by a stem tuber
questions.option_d: binary fission of a root cell
questions.explanation: Potato tubers are modified stems; buds or eyes can grow into new plants through vegetative propagation.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT Biology, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: Which feature distinguishes sexual reproduction from most asexual reproduction?
questions.option_a: Fusion of gametes contributes genetic material from two haploid cells
questions.option_b: It always produces genetically identical offspring
questions.explanation: Sexual reproduction involves gamete formation and fusion, combining genetic material; asexual reproduction typically uses one parent without gamete fusion.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT Biology, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: Which sequence correctly represents early human development after fertilisation?
questions.explanation: After fertilisation, the zygote undergoes cleavage, forms a blastocyst, and then implants in the uterine lining.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT Biology, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: A pregnancy test commonly detects elevated human chorionic gonadotropin (hCG), which is initially secreted by cells associated with the
questions.explanation: Trophoblastic cells of the early conceptus produce hCG, which supports the corpus luteum early in pregnancy.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT Biology, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php
